newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli peace rally draws tens of thousands.
newsitem.headline: Israeli peace rally draws tens of thousands.

text.p: Tens of thousands of Israelis demonstrated on Tuesday against Benjamin Netanyahu's policies as the prime minister attended a crisis summit in Washington called to rescue collapsing Middle East peace.

"There is no light at the end of that tunnel," chanted demonstrators, in reference to a tourist tunnel near Islamic shrines in Jerusalem which Netanyahu opened last week, sparking fierce clashes which killed 57 Palestinians and 15 Israelis.

U.S. President Bill Clinton called Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat to a crisis summit in Washington in an effort to rescue the Middle East peace process from collapsing in the wake of the violence.
Left-wing opposition members called on Netanyahu, who ousted the government of Shimon Peres in May, to implement peace deals Israel signed with the PLO under their watch.

"We want the government of Israel to implement the agreement which it has not implemented in the last three months. If this happens we will be back on track. If not we will be in the streets," Yossi Beilin, a Labour party architect of the Oslo peace accords, told Reuters.
"We can prove to ourselves and the world that the peace is stronger than its opponents," Beilin told the rally.

"If he (Netanyahu) returns (from Washington) without an agreement...we will focus all our efforts...in order to bring him down, bring him down, bring him down!" Yossi Sarid, leader of the left-wing Meretz party, told the roaring crowd.
Peace Now organisers put the crowd at 50,000.
Demonstrators waved pictures of slain prime minister Yitzhak Rabin bearing the slogan "We will not forgive, we will not forget".
Rabin was shot dead at a peace rally last November by a right-wing religious Jew opposed to Rabin's willingness to swap occupied land for peace with the Palestinians.
The rally was held not far from the square where Rabin was assassinated.
